slides.texte_overlay:
How You Become Extremely
Educated In Your 20s.
Read one classic a month. Not just new releases. The books people still read after a hundred years have survived for a reason, and they change how you think.
Visit museums alone. No rush, no group, just you and the pieces that catch your eye. Reading every label of one room teaches more than running through ten.
Learn the basics of a second language. Thirty minutes a day for a year gets you real conversations, and every language opens a new way of seeing the world.
Make learning a daily habit. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a year of tiny lessons adds up to more knowledge than most people gain in a decade.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A year of tiny lessons adds up to more than most people learn in a decade.

slides.texte_overlay: Talk to people who know more than you. Ask your grandparents about history, ask a nurse about the body, ask a carpenter about wood. Everyone is an expert in something.
Watch documentaries instead of reality shows. Same couch, same hour, but you go to bed knowing how volcanoes work, why Rome fell or how the pyramids were built.
Teach what you learn. Explain a new idea to a friend the same week you learn it. Teaching is the fastest way to remember something for good, and your friends learn too.
